purpose: Personal-investment research only. Robotics claims are checked against issuer disclosures and current market evidence before affecting the framework.

framework.summary: Adoption is ranked by task structure and customer payback, not by how human-like the machine looks. The August 2026 evidence does not change the sequence.

waves.name: Structured logistics + fixed industrial automation
waves.why: Controlled environments, repeatable tasks, mature safety practices and measurable labour and throughput ROI.

waves.name: Cobots + mobile manipulation + constrained service robots
waves.why: AI expands task coverage while deployments remain geofenced, supervised and workflow-specific.

waves.name: Industrial humanoids
waves.why: Human-shaped facilities help, but dexterity, reliability, battery life, safety and total cost still need proof.

waves.name: Open-world consumer robots
waves.why: Unstructured environments compound edge cases, liability and price sensitivity.

currentRead.commercialSignal: Warehouse/fixed automation remains the strongest public-market evidence set. Symbotic continues to expand deployments and has added warehouse-operations optimisation capability through ARMS Innovations; Teradyne combines robotics with increasingly AI-linked semiconductor test demand.
currentRead.humanoidSignal: Unitree's Shanghai listing confirms that at least one Chinese humanoid/robotics vendor has reached profitability and international scale. That improves sector credibility but does not establish attractive public-market risk/reward at a 219x projected 2025 earnings IPO valuation.
currentRead.portfolioImplication: Keep component, perception, warehouse and cobot exposure ahead of humanoid-OEM exposure until paid deployments, repeat orders, utilisation and unit economics are consistently visible.

screenedOut.reason: Commercial deployment is real, but current revenue scale and cash-burn economics do not clear the Power Stack bar.
ABB Robotics is strategically relevant, but robotics remains diluted within SoftBank's conglomerate and investment-portfolio risk.

Profitable and commercially credible, but the August 2026 Shanghai IPO valuation around 219x projected 2025 earnings is too aggressive for promotion and the listing remains outside the preferred HK/MY/US market set.

notes: Deployment counts alone are not proof of attractive unit economics.
Component and enabling-layer exposure ranks ahead of humanoid-OEM hype when financial evidence is stronger.
